chosen.title: How To Correctly Perform A Sumo Deadlift
chosen.description:
Learn how to safely and correctly perform a sumo deadlift with our step by step video tutorial. 
 
The sumo deadlift is great compound movement that puts more emphasis on the hips, glutes, and legs and reduces load on the lower back compared to the conventional deadlift. There are benefits to both deadlift variations, so it's a good idea to try both!
 
1. Stand with your shins close to the barbell with your feet wider than shoulder width apart and your toes pointing outwards.
2. Hinge forward at the hip and grab the bar, hands around shoulder width apart. Your core and chest should be strong. 
3. Bring the barbell up by driving your hips forward and extending your knees.
4. Keep the barbell close to your body for a smooth path.
5. Return the barbell to the floor by hinging at the hips and driving your glutes backwards.

candidates.title: The BEST Way to DEADLIFT!! Squat Stance Deadlift vs Conventional and Sumo Deadlifts  #fitness
candidates.description:
Conventional or Sumo? NEITHER! In fact the squat stance deadlift might be the best way to deadlift for many athletes.

The Conventional & Sumo deadlifts both have their downfalls. The conventional deadlift while having the largest range of motion tends to place greater shear force on the spine due to the more bent over torso position. However, this also makes it more conducive for eliciting muscular hypotrophy. Taller lifters with longer legs tend to find this method more challenging due to both biomechanical & mobility restrictions.
The sumo deadlift on the other hand keeps the bar closer to the center of mass, combined with a smaller range of motion and more upright torso position tends to make the variation safer on the spine although less effective for hypertrophy. The ultra wide stance & toe flare can create inflammation in the hips as well as promote dysfunctional & unnatural lower body mechanics. 
In fact many powerlifters who use an excessive toe flare on the squat or sumo deadlift end up destroying their natural lower body mechanics. In fact when you examine the walking gait of many powerlifters they look like an overstuffed cowboy from the wild west who just got off a marathon horse back ride as their hip mechanics are horribly aberrant.
The squat-stance deadlift essentially combines the benefits from both the sumo and conventional deadlift while eliminating the inherent weaknesses of each. 
KEY POINT 1: The squat-stance deadlift is the most natural, safe, & effective deadlift technique for a majority of lifters.
KEY POINT 2: The squat stance deadlift is very conducive for strength & hypertrophy as it typically allows the lifter to handle heaviest loads with safest mechanics.
KEY POINT 3: Ed Coan used a very similar technique (semi sumo or modified sumo deadlift) with great success. There’s no reason why you can’t do the same.

candidates.title: Sumo dumbbell deadlift for STRONG GLUTES 🍑 #strengthtraining #fitness #workout
Master the SUMO DEADLIFT with these Form Tips
candidates.description:
Here are some things to keep in mind when performing sumo deadlifts:

1. Wedge your feet in: place your feet at a comfortable angle, making sure your foot positioning is even on each side. After this step, don’t change your foot positioning any more!

2. Engage your lats/ close your armpits: you can think about pulling your arms in towards you or “closing your armpits” and squeezing your lats. Maintain this position throughout the pull.

3. Pull the slack out of the bar: pull on the bar enough that it’s about to come off of the ground. With heavier weights, this might cause the bar to bend.

4. Push the ground away: in the first half of the lift (until the bar reaches your knees) focus on pushing the floor away as hard as you can.

5. Push your hips forward: after the bar passes your knees, focus on pushing your hips forward to complete the lift.
